_what_this_is: One record per HELD-OUT TEST participant from the frozen twin-vs-persistence experiment, disaggregated. No new model, no new metric, no aggregate recomputed.
_provenance: REAL ANONYMISED LONGITUDINAL DATA - College Experience Study. Predictions are the frozen experiment's own, strictly out-of-sample: these participants were never trained on.
_anonymisation: participants renumbered by a stable digest sort; source identifiers dropped entirely; timestamps converted to day offsets from each person's own first report, so no calendar date is published

_definitions.autocorrelation: lag-1 Pearson correlation between a participant's successive stress reports, restricted to consecutive pairs 1-7 days apart, as defined in aedt/audit/ceiling.py. Descriptive evidence of temporal dependence; not a causal measure.
_definitions.predictability_band: r < 0.15 near-unpredictable · 0.15 <= r <= 0.5 typical · r > 0.5 well-predictable
_definitions.band_source: the thresholds are aedt/audit/ceiling.py's own NEAR_UNPREDICTABLE_BELOW and WELL_PREDICTABLE_ABOVE, the constants behind the published 13% / 17% figures. No new threshold was invented.
_definitions.variability_sd: sample standard deviation of the participant's observed stress values
_definitions.macro_f1: the study's pre-registered primary metric, computed per participant by the frozen experiment's scorer
_definitions.warm_up: the first K observations personalise only and are never scored, per the frozen protocol

_uncertainty: No per-participant confidence intervals are published. The study's intervals come from a participant-clustered bootstrap over the cohort, which does not yield an interval for a single person. Per-participant values are point estimates on small numbers of observations and must be read as such.
_redistribution: The source archive is not redistributed. This file carries summary STATISTICS for every participant and observation series for an illustrative subset only; the complete series stay in results/, which is gitignored and never shipped.
illustrative_rule: the scored participants at the minimum, median and maximum within-person autocorrelation
